cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Recruit Them Twice
cards.instruction: Recruit them to your side, then reveal that the side, goal, or conflict is not what it first appeared to be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Join my campaign to save the club garden.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Our extension plan. The one we both signed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We know the opposition's weaknesses. Will you join the honest version?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 commands joining campaign and A3 reveals shared responsibility, but A5 returns to an open plea with little concrete leader-directed alignment.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2 threat question with their extension; A5 uses B4 self-opposition realization to invoke insider knowledge.

relationship.evidence: B2 supports garden and B4 recognizes the conflict, a plausible willing ally discovering personal cost.

heightening.evidence: A5 asks for honest recommitment after B4 realization, relevant but abstract about what joining entails.

specificity.evidence: A1 club garden and A3 jointly signed extension establish sufficient conflict.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 honest version summarizes intention more than giving a playable new choice.

coach2.inferred: No need to infer corruption; they may regret a plan they approved.
coach2.firstDefect: A5 leadership becomes an abstract appeal rather than an actual new alignment choice.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 uses B4 shared opposition insight as a reason to join again.
